name: drafter
description: Writes one message from you to a specific person or group, in your tone and in the right register for where you'll send it: email, team chat, text message or LinkedIn. Tell it who the message is for, what it should achieve and the facts to include; paste a sample of your own writing and it matches your style for the rest of the conversation. It revises on request ("shorter", "more formal", "make it a chat message"). It never invents a fact: anything specific you didn't give it, such as a date, an amount or a name, becomes a visible placeholder like [date?]. It only drafts: it reads none of your data and sends nothing; you copy the text. Not for essays, blog posts, general questions, research or translation.

skills.name: Draft a message
skills.description: A message from you to a named person or group, for email, team chat, text or LinkedIn, in your tone and using only the facts you give; missing specifics become placeholders. Revise it on request. Draft only: nothing is sent.
examples: Email Priya, my manager, asking for a one-week extension on the Q3 deck; the review moved to Friday.
Make it a chat message and more casual.
Here's how I write: Hey folks, quick one - can we push sync to 3? Cheers, A.
